name: Basic noun gender
definition: Learn the gender with each noun. A final consonant or -й usually marks masculine nouns; -а or -я usually marks feminine nouns; -о or -е usually marks neuter nouns. name: Basic written questions
definition: A yes-no question can retain statement word order and end with a question mark. name: Basic genitive forms
definition: Use the genitive after из for origin, after a naming noun for possession or association, and after нет for absence. name: Numbers and basic time notation
definition: In nominative or inanimate-accusative counting phrases, 1 selects singular, 2-4 select genitive singular, and 5-20 select genitive plural. Learn один, одна, одно and два, две as the supplied gender forms in nominative counting; oblique numeral declension is not taught here. Apply the same supplied-form method to hours and minutes. Read clock notation as HH:MM and the explicitly labeled date format as DD.MM.YYYY. Weekday expressions use the accusative with the preposition for on; month expressions use the prepositional with in; taught season time forms use the instrumental. name: ходил / ездил for past 'went (and came back)'
definition: For a completed visit one usually uses был/была + place, or the past of the indeterminate motion verbs ходить/ездить: вчера я ходил в театр, в прошлом году я ездил в Москву. These forms imply the round trip is over; the direction-specific пошёл/поехал describe the departure and need their own lesson. Learn the supplied forms as given.
form_rules: я ходил, ты ходил, он ходил; она ходила
usage_rules: Use ходил/ездил for 'went to and came back' in past narration.
был/была + place also reports a past location.

examples.gloss: Yesterday I went to the theatre (and came back).

examples.text: В прошлом году я ездил в Москву.
examples.gloss: Last year I went to Moscow (and came back).

name: Reporting speech: сказал / написал, что …
definition: To report what someone said or wrote, use a past speech verb (сказал, написал, спросил) followed by что + a clause. The reported clause keeps its own tense: Мастер сказал, что придёт вечером (said that he will come in the evening); В письме он написал, что заменит деталь (wrote that he will replace the part). Word order in the reported clause is free. This pattern reports statements; questions use спросил, whether-clauses need their own lesson.

examples.gloss: The repairman said that he will come in the evening.
I know that this is important.

name: Вы-form commands: -ите imperatives
definition: Polite requests to one person addressed as Вы use the -ите imperative: посмотрите, подпишите, сверьте, уточните, and with a prefix such as по-: посмотрите. The same verb in the informal ты form ends in -и/-ь (посмотри), which is appropriate only where ты address fits; mixing the forms is a register error, not a grammar error. Add пожалуйста for courtesy; перед отправкой/сверьте belong to written workflow phrasing.
form_rules: perfective stem + -ите: подписать → подпишите, уточнить → уточните
usage_rules: Use the -ите form with clients, elders, and service contacts.
Do not address a Вы contact with the ты imperative.
